title: What responsible lending training do Australian credit staff need?
description: How the NCCP Act and ASIC RG 209 and RG 206 shape responsible lending training for lenders and credit staff in Australia, with a role and evidence matrix.
shortAnswer: Australian credit licensees must ensure their representatives are adequately trained and competent under section 47(1)(g) of the National Consumer Credit Protection Act 2009. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) expects licensees to set their own initial and ongoing training (RG 206), and that training must equip lending staff to apply the Chapter 3 responsible lending obligations explained in RG 209: reasonable inquiries, verification, the not unsuitable assessment and the statutory presumptions.
keyTakeaways: The training duty is section 47(1)(g) of the National Credit Act: representatives must be adequately trained and competent to engage in the licensee's authorized credit activities.
ASIC has generally not prescribed courses: RG 206.22 expects each licensee to decide appropriate initial and ongoing training and embed it in recruitment and training systems.

Fixed settings apply in home lending: a Certificate IV in Finance and Mortgage Broking and 20 hours of CPD a year for third party home loan representatives, and 20 hours of CPD a year for responsible managers.
RG 209, issued December 9, 2019 and updated in March 2025 with guidance on HELP debts, explains the Chapter 3 obligations that lending staff must apply.

Buy now pay later providers have needed an Australian credit licence (the statutory term) since June 10, 2025, and low cost credit contract providers can elect modified responsible lending obligations.
appliesTo: Australian credit licensees, including banks, non-bank lenders and lessors
Credit assistance providers and their credit representatives
Buy now pay later providers, licensed from June 10, 2025
Lending officers, credit assessors, hardship and collections staff, responsible managers

sections.heading: What does the law require for responsible lending training?

blocks.text: The National Consumer Credit Protection Act 2009 (National Credit Act) imposes two competence duties on credit licensees, and responsible lending is the core content both must cover. ASIC's [RG 206 Credit licensing: Competence and training](https://asic.gov.au/regulatory-resources/find-a-document/regulatory-guides/rg-206-credit-licensing-competence-and-training/) summarizes them: licensees must meet the organizational competence obligation in section 47(1)(f), and "must also ensure that your representatives are adequately trained and competent to engage in the credit activities authorised by your licence: s47(1)(g)".

The obligations staff must apply sit in Chapter 3 of the Act. ASIC's [responsible lending page](https://asic.gov.au/regulatory-resources/credit/responsible-lending/) states the key concept: licensees "must not enter into a credit contract with a consumer, suggest a credit contract to a consumer or assist a consumer to apply for a credit contract if the credit contract is unsuitable for the consumer", and "must decide how you will meet the responsible lending obligations". [RG 209 Credit licensing: Responsible lending conduct](https://asic.gov.au/regulatory-resources/find-a-document/regulatory-guides/rg-209-credit-licensing-responsible-lending-conduct/) sets out ASIC's views on what Chapter 3 requires.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects RG 209 (issued December 9, 2019, with paragraphs RG 209.68 to RG 209.69 added in March 2025), RG 206 (issued April 1, 2020) and ASIC's credit pages as at November 2026.

sections.heading: What training does ASIC expect credit licensees to provide?

blocks.text: ASIC leaves most training design to the licensee but sets fixed minimums in home lending and for responsible managers. RG 206.22 says ASIC has generally not set specific training requirements for representatives and that licensees should "determine for yourself what is appropriate initial and ongoing training" and "embed this in your recruitment and training systems". RG 206.25 adds that where industry training standards exist for a sector or product, ASIC expects representatives to be trained to at least that level.

items: **Third party home loan representatives (brokers):** at least a Certificate IV in Finance and Mortgage Broking and at least 20 hours of CPD a year (RG 206.23(a)). The [mortgage broker best interests duty page](/regulations/mortgage-broker-best-interests-duty-training) covers this group in detail.

**Representatives giving home loan assistance on their own licensee's products (for example bank lending staff):** training in a form the licensee decides that lets them apply the knowledge in RG 206 Table 2, plus either 20 hours of CPD a year or a regular knowledge update review with sufficient CPD to complete it (RG 206.23(b)).

**Responsible managers:** at least two years of relevant problem free experience and a Certificate IV level credit qualification or a relevant higher qualification (RG 206.7), and at least 20 hours of CPD a year (RG 206.12(b)). RG 206.72 says their CPD should include compliance training, which "would need to encompass the responsible lending obligations".

blocks.text: RG 206 Table 2 lists the training outcomes for own product home loan representatives: dealing appropriately with consumers (gathering their personal and financial situation and addressing their priorities), knowledge of home loan products and their characteristics, and the economic and market context including interest rates and real estate concepts. The broader AFS equivalent is covered on the [ASIC RG 105 organizational competence](/regulations/asic-rg-105-organisational-competence) page.

sections.heading: Which responsible lending obligations must lending staff be able to apply?

blocks.text: Lending staff must be able to carry out each step in RG 209's summary of key obligations (Table 6), because each is a separate statutory duty. The table below summarizes them with the section references RG 209 gives for credit providers.

blocks.text: Two RG 209 themes deserve particular training time. First, scalability: RG 209.83 says determining what inquiries and steps are reasonable requires staff to "apply your own judgment" in the circumstances, so scenario practice matters more than memorized rules. Second, benchmarks: RG 209.136 warns that income and expense benchmarks do not provide information about the actual consumer, and RG 209.140 expects licensees using expense benchmarks to use the most up to date version and a realistic figure.

sections.heading: How do responsible lending duties map to roles, frequency and evidence?

blocks.text: A matrix that ties each role to its Chapter 3 tasks and to file level evidence makes section 47(1)(g) demonstrable. The table below is original and illustrative. Apart from the 20 hour CPD settings, ASIC does not fix frequencies, so the frequency column is a design choice the licensee would need to justify. The guide on [building a training matrix for a bank](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix-for-a-bank) shows the wider structure.

blocks.text: Records serve both purposes. RG 209.265 says that failing to keep a record of inquiries, verification steps and the information relied on "may make it difficult for you to adequately demonstrate" compliance, and RG 209.267 notes that fact find and needs analysis tools give structure "especially where you conduct business through a number of credit representatives". Those same files are the best evidence that training is applied. The guide on [preparing training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) covers register design.

sections.heading: What changed for buy now pay later and hardship teams?

blocks.text: Buy now pay later (BNPL) staff are now inside the licensing and training regime. ASIC's [BNPL licensing page](https://asic.gov.au/regulatory-resources/credit/buy-now-pay-later-credit-contracts-credit-licensing/) says that from June 10, 2025 anyone engaging in credit activities involving BNPL contracts must hold an Australian credit licence. BNPL contracts that meet the definition of a low cost credit contract can elect to comply with modified responsible lending obligations from that date; other BNPL contracts are regulated like other credit. BNPL providers therefore owe the same section 47(1)(g) training duty, with content matched to whichever responsible lending regime they apply.

Hardship and collections staff need the dispute timeframes as well as the lending rules. Under ASIC's RG 271, credit complaints involving default notices, hardship notices or requests to postpone enforcement must receive an IDR response within 21 calendar days. The [RG 271 complaints training page](/regulations/asic-rg-271-complaints-handling-training) explains those requirements, and [financial services](/industries/financial-services) covers related obligations.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models the Chapter 3 obligations, the RG 209 guidance and each lending role as a structured framework, then links every role to the concepts and assessment points it must demonstrate before receiving lending authority. When ASIC updates RG 209, as it did in March 2025, the changed paragraphs identify which roles and assessments need revision, and each record shows the version a person was assessed against.

faqs.q: Do bank lending staff need a Certificate IV in Finance and Mortgage Broking?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. RG 206.23 requires the Certificate IV for representatives providing third party home loan credit assistance. Staff who only provide home loan assistance on their own licensee's products may complete training the licensee decides is appropriate, provided it lets them apply the RG 206 Table 2 knowledge, plus annual CPD or a knowledge update review.

faqs.q: Does ASIC prescribe responsible lending training hours for all credit staff?
faqs.a: No. Outside home lending and responsible managers, RG 206.22 says ASIC has generally not set specific training requirements and expects each licensee to determine appropriate initial and ongoing training. The 20 hour CPD settings apply to home loan representatives and to responsible managers.

RG 209 is ASIC guidance on how it interprets Chapter 3 of the National Credit Act and the steps licensees can take to reduce the risk of non-compliance. The obligations themselves are in the Act. Training should teach the statutory obligations and use RG 209 to explain how ASIC expects them to be applied.

faqs.q: What did the March 2025 update to RG 209 change?
faqs.a: ASIC added RG 209.68 to RG 209.69 to give guidance on how HELP debts are treated in assessing a consumer's financial situation, renumbered the following paragraphs and amended RG 209.70. Training content that cites RG 209 paragraph numbers after RG 209.67 should be checked for the new numbering.
